column3: This process map covers the phases commonly involved in civil litigation. It aims to be relevant across different litigation systems and national traditions so as to enable them to be handled and analysed in a like-for-like way. Civil law systems, for example, do not organise proceedings into trial and pre-trial in the way that common law systems do. Process maps for particular types of litigation will inevitably have differences from this generic process map but can be mapped to it. Phases in specific litigation matters can be based on this process map or, where available, the process map for a particular litigation type.

Covers exchange of information and positions before court proceeding and initiation of court proceedings. Settlement proposals are excluded (see Settlement phase). Disputes about procedural failures to commence correctly belong here; disputes about jurisdiction belong in Related proceedings. Entry of judgment in default of appearance or defence is included here. The initial exchange of claims/counterclaims, defences/answers and other pleadings is included; subsequent rounds belong in Pleadings and evidence.

column3: Covers establishment of the procedure, timetable and (if applicable) budget, interim measures, and resolution of issues arising other than the merits of the case. Summary determinations belong in Resolving the merits. Applications about evidence (eg document production) are included here; gathering evidence is in Pleadings and evidence.

column3: Covers preparation and exchange of all evidence and (where applicable) memorials. Pleadings and evidence are combined in a single phase to accommodate the variety of ways in which these topics are addressed in different systems. This phase includes memorials as used in some courts. Initial exchanges of claims and answers belong in Commencement. Live examination of witnesses at trial belongs in Resolving the merits. Evidence prepared solely for Case management is excluded.

column3: Covers presentation of the substantive issues in the case to the court and obtaining decisions on those issues and on costs. This phase will often involve one or more hearings but not necessarily in all systems. In a common law system it includes trials but also other methods of resolving the substance of a case, such as summary judgment, summary decree or strike-out.

column3: Covers seeking an agreed resolution of substantive issues in the case. This is a standing phase that runs throughout the matter.

column3: Covers challenges to the bringing of proceedings, challenges to the judge's involvement (recusal), enforcement of judgments, orders or other decisions, and challenges to those decisions. Challenges to jurisdiction / venue / forum are included here. If related proceedings in a different forum are likely to be complex, consider opening a separate matter or sub-matter.
